sources.note: Bibliographic: holdings are Glottolog 5.0 and Ethnologue entries only; no archival deposits (no PARADISEC, no SIL archive item) for ygm.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page yago1240 'Tanda-Yagomi' and reference records 568952 (van den Berg) and 673588 (Carter et al. 2023)
sources.note: Bibliographic only: three references in total (Z'graggen 1975 overview, van den Berg list post, Carter et al. 2023 survey); zero grammar/phonology/sketch entries.

sources.citation: Language & Linguistics in Melanesia, vols 38-44 (2020-2026) and special issues, tables of contents (scanned for Tandɨ/Yagomi/Warup/Suter)
sources.note: No paper on Tandɨ or the Warup languages found (Suter items are Asmat-Muli 2020 and Huon benefactives 2024).

sources.citation: O'Bannon, Devin (SIL Global). 2025. ISO 639-3 Registration Authority Change Request 2025-042: Update language name [ygm] Yagomi to Tandɨ; retain the name Yagomi (LCA note: reference name revised to 'Tanda'). Dallas: SIL Global / ISO 639-3 RA. 2 pp.
sources.note: Nothing: a two-page name-change request with rationale, LCA note ('The language is called Tanda, pronounced [tandə]' after van den Berg 2020) and three references; no wordlist, transcription or prosodic remark. Useful only as an identity document (ygm = Tandɨ = Z'graggen's Yagomi) and as confirmation that SIL's own 2025 knowledge of the language rests entirely on Carter et al. 2023.

sources.citation: Carter, Jed, Beautlyn Eliab, Karl Kama, Roger Maikei, Devin O'Bannon & Napa Yanderave. 2023. Survey Report for Uma (Ronji) [roe], Tandɨ (Yagomi) [ygm], Muratayak [asx], Degenang (Degenan) [dge], and Forak [frq] Languages. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2023-003. Dallas: SIL International. 71 pp.
sources.note: Nothing: the words stress/accent/tone/syllable do not occur and there are zero IPA stress marks in the report. Sec. 2.1.4 (p.10): 120-item SIL-PNG list 'transcribed using the International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA) and.. digitally recorded'. App. D Table 37 (pp.55-64) 'Tandɨ (Yagomi)' column (dɔman 'his head', mɛruan 'hair', tɛndɔmna 'nose', dalaŋ 'eye', mɛvalaŋ 'tooth', walik 'woman', umɡak 'man', manam 'bird') carries no stress marking. Sec. 3.1.1.2 (pp.15-16): Tandɨ = clan 'private language' in Yagomi, 20-30 older speakers, EGIDS 8a; Suter (p.c.) matched it to Z'graggen's unpublished Yagomi…

sources.citation: van den Berg, René. 2020 [Glottolog year '2010' is a typo]. New highly endangered language discovered in PNG. Post to the PapuanLanguages discussion list (ANU), 17 March 2020.
sources.note: Nothing on prosody. States the name is 'Tanda, pronounced [tandə]', spoken only in Yagomi village as a secret clan language by ~10 families, 'probably a Finisterre-Huon language'; SIL collected a 170-item wordlist with recordings; 22 sample words given without stress marks.
sources.venue: New highly endangered language discovered in PNG

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew & Harald Hammarström. 2018. The Trans New Guinea family. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide (The World of Linguistics 4), 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. (Warup data-coverage listing, ch. 2 appendix.)
sources.note: No phonology content for Yagomi: the entry records that the best available source in 2018 was Z'graggen's 1975 overview (no wordlist, sketch or phonology), which independently confirms the empty descriptive record.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Rai Coast languages, Madang Province, PNG. Pacific Linguistics D-30.
sources.note: Not a source for this language: Yagomi appears only as 'A7' on the language map (D-30 covers the Madang Rai Coast stock; B11 there is Yabong). Intro sec. 7 describes a 'semiphonemic' transcription and says nothing about stress.

sources.citation: McElhanon, Kenneth A. 1975. North-eastern Trans-New Guinea Phylum languages. In Wurm (ed.), PL C-38: 527-567.
sources.note: Nothing; checklist entry only: '2.8.1.3.7.7. Yagomi (WR-53), pop. 140. Warup Census Division: Yagomi. The people of this village were reported as speaking the ASAT language by Claassen (Claassen and McElhanon 1970).'

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1975. The Languages of the Madang District, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics B-41. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing; checklist/classification only: 'WARUP FAMILY.. A7 Yagomi 137' (Yagomi village, 1973 census) and language map. The words stress/accent do not occur in the volume.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In Stephen A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea area languages and language study, vol. 1: Papuan languages and the New Guinea linguistic scene (Pacific Linguistics C-38), 569-612. Canberra: Australian National University. [ANU Open Research hdl 1885/252971, chapter PDF 6.8 MB + extracted text 110 KB]
sources.note: No phonology content for Yagomi: the only occurrence of the name in the chapter (ANU extracted text, line 438) is the map legend 'WARUP FAMtlY A7 Yagomi' [scanned for FAMILY]; the chapter contains no wordlist or sound-system notes for any Warup language and the words stress/accent/tone/tonal/pitch do not occur anywhere in it.
sources.venue: New Guinea area languages and language study

sources.note: Nothing; stub giving 20 speakers (2020), Warup < Finisterre, Yagomi village; cites Ethnologue only.
